Q1.answer: Forecasting models (apparently time-series forecasters, TSF) whose inputs are z-scored with statistics fixed from some reference data (TSD, apparently training data) become mis-scaled and lose accuracy when the level of the series shifts (LS) after deployment. The paper asks whether re-estimating normalization moments per input window (RWN) removes this error without hurting accuracy when there is no shift.
Q1.missing: None of the acronyms (TSF, TSD, LS, PCM, OOD, IID, RWN) are expanded; the reading above is inferred from context.

Q2.answer: Deployed forecasting systems reportedly encounter level shifts, and standard pipelines normalize with fixed training statistics, so post-shift inputs are mis-scaled and error inflates.
Q2.missing: Both supporting statements are [CITATION NEEDED] placeholders; no evidence of prevalence or cost of level shifts is given.

Q3.answer: The authors claim that prior evaluations confound moment staleness with insufficient model capacity, so it is unclear whether gains from re-normalization come from fresher statistics or something else.
Q3.missing: The claim is tagged '[CITATION NEEDED: literature search not yet run]'; no prior approach is named or described.

Q4.answer: On a synthetic hourly series generator (SynthLoad: daily and weekly cycles plus white Gaussian noise), they inject level shifts of 0.2-0.8 sigma after the training period and compare an MLP forecaster (h=64, input 168, horizon 24) normalized with (a) training-period moments, (b) moments from the trailing 48 steps (RWN), and (c) moments re-estimated once after the shift then frozen (RWN-F). 5 seeds, MAE mean +/- sd on the test period.
Q4.missing: What 'PCM', 'iso-budget' and 'capacity-matched' mean operationally; whether the RWN re-normalization is inverted on outputs; train/test period lengths; where in the test period the shift occurs.

Q5.answer: Per-window normalization is meant to track the current level so inputs are no longer mis-scaled; capacity matching is used to rule out model size as an explanation; RWN-F is used to separate one-shot re-estimation from continuous adaptation.
Q5.missing: No explicit rationale for the trailing-48 window or for why capacity matching (rather than varying capacity) would deconfound staleness from capacity.

Q6.answer: No-shift (IID) comparison of baseline vs RWN; level-shift comparisons at s = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 sigma for baseline vs RWN; an RWN-F ablation at 0.6 sigma only. All with one MLP backbone and 5 seeds.

Q7.answer: At s = 0.6 sigma MAE drops from 0.641 (baseline) to 0.452 (RWN), about 29%; across 0.2-0.6 sigma reductions are 11-29% with sd <= 0.012; no-shift MAE is 0.409 +/- 0.007 vs 0.412 +/- 0.006.
Q7.missing: Numeric values for 0.2 and 0.4 sigma are not reported; Figure 1 is described but not shown.

Q8.answer: On this synthetic generator, with this one MLP and untuned window, per-window normalization reduces MAE under moderate level shifts without measurable cost when there is no shift; in the single 0.6 sigma ablation, roughly two thirds of the gain survives freezing the moments after one re-estimation.

Q9.answer: Not established: any benefit on real data, other backbones or sizes, other drift types (variance, seasonality), or at 0.8 sigma; that capacity is not a factor (capacity was fixed, never varied); that the one-third adaptivity share holds at other shift sizes; statistical equivalence at no-shift.

Q10.answer: Controlled synthetic evidence that per-window moment re-estimation reduces MAE 11-29% under moderate level shifts at no-shift parity, a boundary at 0.8 sigma, and an ablation attributing about one third of the gain to continued adaptation.

Q11.answer: Synthetic data only; single small MLP with fixed capacity; untuned 48-step window; only level shifts; 5 seeds without formal tests; ablation at one shift size; unexplained breakdown at 0.8 sigma; missing citations.

Q12.answer: Re-normalizing each input window with its own recent statistics largely removes the error caused by moderate level shifts in a synthetic setting, costs nothing when there is no shift, stops helping at large shifts, and most of the gain comes from simply re-estimating the statistics once.

location.quote: Z-scored TSF pipelines with TSD-anchored moments are brittle under OOD LS regimes

findings.observed: The problem statement is packed with unexpanded acronyms (TSF, TSD, OOD, LS, IID) and is never restated in plain terms.
findings.reader_struggle: The audience is explicitly not forecasting specialists; they must guess that TSD means training data and LS means level shift.
findings.likely_consequence: Adjacent readers may understand the problem only after reading the Setup, or misread which statistics are 'anchored'.
findings.revision_principle: State the problem once in plain language, expanding every acronym at first use, before compressing it.

location.quote: Deployed TSF systems encounter LS [CITATION NEEDED: prevalence of level shifts in deployed load forecasting]

findings.observed: Both motivating premises (level shifts are common; fixed-statistic normalization is standard) are unsupported placeholders.
findings.reader_struggle: A verifying reviewer has no evidence the problem occurs in practice or that the criticised practice is standard.
findings.likely_consequence: The work reads as solving a hypothetical problem; importance is taken on faith.
findings.revision_principle: Ground each motivating premise in cited evidence or a concrete example before relying on it.

location.quote: RQ1: does RWN reduce LS-regime MAE with IID parity? RQ2: what fraction of the gain

findings.observed: Two explicit RQs are given and map onto the experiments, but are phrased in acronyms; 'RQ1b' is later cited without being defined.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must decode acronyms and infer that RQ1b is the no-shift parity part.
findings.likely_consequence: The questions are recoverable but with friction; mismatch between 'RQ1b' and the stated RQs causes brief confusion.
findings.revision_principle: Phrase research questions in plain terms and label any sub-questions where they are introduced.

location.quote: Contributions: (1) capacity-matched evidence of 11–29% MAE reduction under LS up to 0.6σ

findings.observed: Contributions are listed concretely and scoped, but novelty relative to existing per-window normalization practice is not established because related work is absent.
findings.reader_struggle: A domain expert cannot tell whether per-window normalization is new or the contribution is only the controlled evaluation.
findings.likely_consequence: Experts may discount the contribution as re-testing a known technique.
findings.revision_principle: Position the contribution against named prior methods and say explicitly what is new: the technique or the controlled evidence.

location.quote: We inject PCM LS of magnitude s ∈ {0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8}σ post-TSD.

findings.observed: Key method terms are undefined (PCM, iso-budget, capacity-matched, what sigma refers to); train/test lengths, shift timing, and whether outputs are de-normalized with window moments are not stated.
findings.reader_struggle: An adjacent researcher cannot reproduce or even fully picture the pipeline; the 'capacity matching' that supposedly deconfounds is not explained.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers cannot judge whether the comparison is fair or replicate it.
findings.revision_principle: Define each procedural term operationally and give enough detail (splits, shift timing, normalization/inversion) for replication.

location.quote: RWN-F at 0.6σ: 0.518

findings.observed: One synthetic generator, one backbone, 5 seeds; the RWN-F ablation is run (or reported) at a single shift magnitude with no sd; capacity is never varied despite being the proposed alternative explanation.
findings.reader_struggle: Experts see that the design cannot test the capacity-vs-staleness question it poses, and the attribution rests on one condition.
findings.likely_consequence: The one-third attribution and the staleness conclusion appear fragile.
findings.revision_principle: Design experiments so each claimed attribution is tested by manipulating the factor in question, across more than one condition.

location.quote: At s = 0.6σ, 0.641 → 0.452; across 0.2–0.6σ the reduction is 11–29%

findings.observed: Headline numbers are given with sd for IID and 0.8 sigma, but values for 0.2 and 0.4 sigma and all sds for the 0.6 sigma pair are only summarised; the order of the pair at 0.8 sigma is ambiguous.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot verify the 11% end of the range or tell which number is RWN at 0.8 sigma.
findings.likely_consequence: Results are believed approximately but not verifiable.
findings.revision_principle: Report every condition's mean and spread for every method in one place, with consistent method ordering.

location.quote: moment staleness rather than capacity plausibly dominates LS error here, though capacity was fixed, not varied

findings.observed: The discussion appropriately hedges, but does not explain why RWN jumps from near-IID MAE at 0.6 sigma to about 0.71 at 0.8 sigma, which is itself informative about the mechanism.
findings.reader_struggle: Experts expect per-window normalization to be roughly shift-invariant; the abrupt failure is left uninterpreted.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers are unsure whether the mechanism story is right.
findings.revision_principle: Interpret anomalous results that bear on the proposed mechanism rather than only reporting them.

location.quote: Caveats: synthetic-only, untuned window, LS-only (no variance or seasonality drift).

findings.observed: Limitations are disclosed clearly and the 0.8 sigma boundary is stated honestly; the single-condition ablation and fixed capacity are only partly acknowledged.
findings.reader_struggle: Mostly clear; the scope of the ablation limitation must be inferred.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers correctly bound the synthetic scope but may over-generalise the one-third figure.
findings.revision_principle: List every design restriction that bounds a headline claim, including single-condition ablations.

location.quote: Moment staleness and capacity insufficiency are confounded in the evaluations we examined

findings.observed: The story (problem, RQs, results, boundary, ablation) is consistent, but the capacity-vs-staleness framing introduced as the central gap is not actually tested, so the arc does not close.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers wait for a capacity manipulation that never comes.
findings.likely_consequence: The 'deconfounding' thread feels unresolved.
findings.revision_principle: Frame the narrative around what the experiments can actually resolve.

location.quote: RWN for LS-Robust TSF Under PCM Drift

findings.observed: Title and abstract use at least eight unexpanded acronyms (RWN, LS, TSF, PCM, TSD, OOD, IID, AWGN) plus 'hebdomadal'; none is defined anywhere.
findings.reader_struggle: The stated audience lacks forecasting-specific vocabulary; even experts must guess PCM and TSD.
findings.likely_consequence: Binding adjacent readers are lost at the title and abstract.
findings.revision_principle: Expand every acronym at first use and prefer plain words for terms the audience is not assumed to know.

findings.observed: Sections follow a sensible order and results are keyed to RQs, but steps are compressed and some references (RQ1b, Figure 1) point to things not present.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must reconstruct links between claims and conditions.
findings.likely_consequence: Flow is followable with effort.
findings.revision_principle: Make every cross-reference resolve to something defined in the text.

location.quote: across 0.2–0.6σ the reduction is 11–29%, with sd ≤ 0.012

findings.observed: The 11-29% range and the 'monotonic' baseline growth depend on numbers and a figure that are not presented; four citation placeholders remain.
findings.reader_struggle: A verifying reviewer can check only the 0.6 sigma and 0.8 sigma points.
findings.likely_consequence: Most of the headline range must be taken on trust.
findings.revision_principle: Every quantitative claim should point to a reported number, table, or visible figure.

location.quote: Figure 1. RWN stays near IID MAE up to 0.6σ, whereas the baseline degrades monotonically.

findings.observed: Only a caption is present; the figure itself and any table of per-condition results are absent.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot inspect the trend, error bars, or the 0.2/0.4 sigma values.
findings.likely_consequence: The core evidence is invisible.
findings.revision_principle: Include the actual figure or a table with all conditions and spreads, and make the caption state what to look for.

location.quote: An RWN-F ablation isolates the adaptive-moment term at about one third of the gain.

findings.observed: The one-third share is arithmetically consistent at 0.6 sigma ((0.518-0.452)/(0.641-0.452) ~ 0.35) but is stated generally from a single condition without spread; the parity and range claims mostly match what is shown.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers may take 'about one third' as a general property.
findings.likely_consequence: Over-generalisation of the ablation result.
findings.revision_principle: State each attribution with the conditions it was measured under and its uncertainty.

location.quote: Under capacity matching, LS-induced MAE inflation appears to be mostly moment staleness.

findings.observed: The staleness-over-capacity conclusion is drawn although capacity was never varied; the claim that prior evaluations confound these factors rests on an unrun literature search.
findings.reader_struggle: Verifiers cannot see how fixed capacity rules capacity out.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers may accept a mechanistic conclusion the design cannot support.
findings.revision_principle: Restrict mechanistic conclusions to factors that were actually manipulated.

location.quote: RWN removes most of it for moderate LS at IID parity, but not at 0.8σ.

findings.observed: Headline numbers recur in abstract, contributions, discussion and conclusion, but briefly; no harmful repetition.
findings.reader_struggle: Minimal; repetition reinforces the key finding.
findings.likely_consequence: Key result is remembered.
findings.revision_principle: Keep repetition to the core claim and use the saved space for missing definitions.

location.quote: Backbone: MLP (h = 64, L = 168, H = 24), iso-budget, 5 seeds

findings.observed: Extreme compression: acronyms, symbols (h, L, H, s, sigma) and design choices are delivered in telegraphic fragments with no definitions.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must hold many undefined symbols simultaneously and decode them from context.
findings.likely_consequence: Adjacent readers give up or misunderstand the setup.
findings.revision_principle: Introduce one new concept at a time and define symbols where they appear.

location.quote: Canonical pipelines apply TSD-anchored z-scoring

findings.observed: No sentence tells a non-forecasting reader what the normalization practice is, what the benchmark is, or what a level shift looks like, though the audience file says these cannot be assumed.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers lack the background needed to appreciate why the baseline fails.
findings.likely_consequence: The significance of the result is not grasped by the intended audience.
findings.revision_principle: Supply the minimal background the stated audience lacks before presenting the method.

location.quote: Non-synthetic validation remains open.

findings.observed: The practical implication (should practitioners use per-window normalization? when does it fail?) is not stated; the conclusion ends on an open item.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must infer the takeaway for their own work.
findings.likely_consequence: The finding is remembered as a narrow synthetic result without guidance.
findings.revision_principle: State the practical implication for the reader, bounded by the tested conditions.

inference_issues.claim_text: Under capacity matching, LS-induced MAE inflation appears to be mostly moment staleness.
inference_issues.missing_link: Capacity was held fixed, not varied, so no evidence separates capacity from staleness; the same claim appears in the abstract ('moment staleness, not representational capacity, dominates').

inference_issues.claim_text: Moment staleness and capacity insufficiency are confounded in the evaluations we examined [CITATION NEEDED: literature search not yet run]
inference_issues.missing_link: No evaluations are cited or described; the gap claim rests on a literature search the placeholder says was not run.

inference_issues.claim_text: An RWN-F ablation isolates the adaptive-moment term at about one third of the gain.
inference_issues.missing_link: RWN-F is reported only at 0.6 sigma, with no sd; 'isolates' and the general one-third share are not supported across conditions.

inference_issues.claim_text: across 0.2–0.6σ the reduction is 11–29%, with sd ≤ 0.012, so ordering is seed-stable
inference_issues.missing_link: Values for 0.2 and 0.4 sigma and the figure are not shown; seed stability is asserted from sd without per-condition numbers or a test.
Parity is inferred from overlapping means with 5 seeds; no equivalence margin or test is given.

inference_issues.claim_text: We deconfound them via capacity matching.
inference_issues.missing_link: Capacity matching is not defined, and matching capacity across normalization variants does not by itself test whether capacity insufficiency contributes to shift error.

objective_discrepancies: The objective asks whether per-window normalization reduces error under level shift without harming no-shift accuracy; the paper conveys this, but only to readers who can decode the acronyms, which the stated audience cannot be assumed to do.
The objective emphasizes 'how much of any gain depends on continuing to adapt those statistics'; the paper answers this only at one shift magnitude, while presenting it as a general one-third figure.
The objective does not mention capacity vs staleness, yet the paper frames this as the central gap and draws a conclusion about it that its design cannot support.

The objective wants the reader to know 'where the finding stops'; the paper states the 0.8 sigma boundary and synthetic scope clearly, which matches, but does not explain why the method fails at 0.8 sigma.
